input.question: Why aren’t we allowed to lower the salaries of politicians? So that we can be sure that they are running not for money but because they really want to serve?
input.ground_truth: Mostly because it would become a tool to control the have-nots. Lower the the salaries of politicians until it a burden even for those who want to serve. Net result is that the only people who would run wouldn't be the people who want to serve, but the people who are financially able. Side note. Most of the money politician make come from things other than their salary. Book deals, speeches, etc...

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why aren’t we allowed to lower the salaries of politicians? So that we can be sure that they are running not for money but because they really want to serve?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you have a big job, like being the leader of a big playground. If someone says, “I’ll only play if you give me extra snacks,” then they might not really want to help make the playground fun for everyone—they might just want the snacks.

If we let grown-ups who work in government get paid less or nothing, some people might only want the job for the money (or to not lose money), and not because they really want to help everyone.

But if we pay them a fair salary, then we can be more sure that they are taking the job because they really want to help people, not just because it pays a lot or nothing at all.

So, we don’t lower their salaries too much, so we know they are working because they care, not just for money.
